items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: my favorite trumpet player by that time was Bunny Berigan. He was my idol. And when I heard Bunny I just said well that’s it. But Bunny’s favorite was Louis. And that’s what they told me, they said, “Where do you think he learned to play from?”

ctx.x: Right, okay. I wanted to ask you something, you were taking about listening to Louis Armstrong, and that you considered those records to be older stuff, that you had to go back and listen to. But this was late 1930s you were talking about, right? And Louis had recorded those records only about ten years before that. Is that right? So it really wasn’t that big a space between the time when you had to go back and listen to him, it was only ten years, is that right? So really it kind of wasn’t that old.

Well what kind of burned those guys up a little bit, the ones that were talking about the old Louis, my favorite trumpet player by that time was Bunny Berigan. He was my idol. And when I heard Bunny I just said well that’s it. But Bunny’s favorite was Louis. And that’s what they told me, they said, “Where do you think he learned to play from?” So you learn, a little bit at a time.
Well you were getting your Louis through Bunny, then, right?

items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Artie had told me and some of those guys that I didn’t hear enough of the early Louis Armstrongs, which I didn’t. And meantime I had bought a lot of those records and listened to them

ctx.x: So you never at that point got into the New York Local. Because they just pulled your card and you had to start over?

Well in a way I’m glad I didn’t. You know, because the way it turned out it was good. And you get mad — I got mad at Artie. He had a recording date and this was in the 1937 band, September. And I’d been in that band too. But after the union card thing, I was not too friendly. So he had one of those transcription dates in New York. Like we’d play in Wildwood, New Jersey, a summer resort, and this was September I guess, at the end of the summer. And there was a new tune out, I can’t remember the name of it, and my…
You did some traveling in the south with Artie Shaw? When Billie Holiday was in the band, didn’t you?
